messages.text: New champion Antonelli tops Brazil practice

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli completed an impressive first day back on track as F1's new world champion to set the pace in second practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest for Mercedes in second practice at Interlagos ahead of Lando Norris in upgraded McLaren | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest for Mercedes in second practice at Interlagos ahead of Lando Norris in upgraded McLaren F1's new world champion sets the pace from its outgoing one on the first day in Brazil; Max Verstappen third fastest but Ferraris off pace on short runs; Rain forecast over weekend; watch final practice at 2.30pm ahead Qualifying at 6pm live on Sky Sports F1 on Saturday Friday 6 November 2026 21:16, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Kimi Antonelli completed an impressive first day back on track as F1's new world champion to set the pace in second practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Five days after becoming the sport's youngest title winner in Mexico, Antonelli followed up his second-fastest time from first practice with the quickest of the more representative second session around the undulating Interlagos lap. Antonelli was the only driver to lap below 71 seconds with his benchmark time of 1:10.763 proving two tenths of a second quicker than nearest challengers Lando Norris, the P1 pacesetter , and Max Verstappen. messages.text: Patriots' Henderson sidelined by 'unexplained neurological symptoms'

metadata.summary: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson says a series of "unexplained neurological symptoms" are the reason for his recent absence.
metadata.content: NFL: New England Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson has been absent due to 'unexplained neurological symptoms' | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NFL: New England Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson has been absent due to 'unexplained neurological symptoms' TreVeyon Henderson reveals on social media that he has spent several days in hospital; cause of symptoms still unknown but 24-year-old says results have been "reassuring"; Henderson missed the New England Patriots' win over the Miami Dolphins last weekend Friday 6 November 2026 19:46, UK Image: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson has been absent due to 'unexplained neurological symptoms' New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson says a series of "unexplained neurological symptoms" are the reason for his recent absence. Henderson has not practised since late October, when he was listed as having an illness, and missed Sunday's 24-19 victory over the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. The player revealed in a social media post on Friday that he has spent a number of days in hospital after issues with his strength and coordination. The cause of the problem remains "unknown and unexplainable", although Henderson says results have been "reassuring". metadata.summary: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says he reminded Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc that the team comes first after their first-lap clash in Mexico in a meeting ahead of this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur confirms Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc meeting after Mexico clash ahead of Sao Paulo GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur confirms Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc meeting after Mexico clash ahead of Sao Paulo GP Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc and Frederic Vasseur spoke on Thursday evening at Interlagos four days on from team-mates' first-lap incident in Mexico; Vasseur says "the message was clear and will stay clear"; watch Qualifying at 6pm live on Sky Sports F1 on Saturday Friday 6 November 2026 19:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur answers questions about Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after a public spat between the two Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur says he reminded Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc that the team comes first after their first-lap clash in Mexico in a meeting ahead of this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix. The lap-one incident between the Ferrari drivers in last Sunday's race, which saw both cars run wide track at Turn Four in battle for the lead, ultimately opened the door for Red Bull's Max Verstappen to win the race. Hamilton has subsequently been critical of Leclerc in interviews and said that discussions were required to more clearly define their rules of combat to avoid costly repeats in future. metadata.summary: Jamie George says England's players were "hurt" by a newspaper report of a rift with head coach Steve Borthwick in the summer, calling the timing of the article "shocking" ahead of Sunday's Nations Championship clash with Australia.
metadata.content: England rugby: Jamie George says squad 'hurt' by article that reported rift with Steve Borthwick this summer | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive England rugby: Jamie George says squad 'hurt' by article that reported rift with Steve Borthwick this summer Jamie George insists the England squad "are all massively behind Steve [Borthwick] in every way possible" as they prepare for Nations Championship game vs Australia on Sunday; England squad addressed media reports of issues between players and coach Friday 6 November 2026 18:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England hooker Jamie George told Sky Sports News there is no rift between players and head coach Steve Borthwick Jamie George says England's players were "hurt" by a newspaper report of a rift with head coach Steve Borthwick in the summer, calling the timing of the article "shocking" ahead of Sunday's Nations Championship clash with Australia. The Times reported that some England players lost faith in Borthwick during a summer campaign with included a 45-21 defeat to world champions South Africa and a nervy win over Argentina. It is alleged players objected to Borthwick's treatment of them, that he was involved in a training ground bust-up with Ellis Genge and that they wanted RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney - who this week unequivocally backed the head coach - to listen to their gripes. messages.text: Carrick: 'Not impossible' Man Utd can achieve Ferguson success again

metadata.summary: Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can reach the heights achieved under Sir Alex Ferguson but is not expecting the same level of patience.
metadata.content: Michael Carrick: Manchester United boss says it is possible club can emulate Sir Alex Ferguson's success at Old Trafford | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Michael Carrick: Manchester United boss says it is possible club can emulate Sir Alex Ferguson's success at Old Trafford Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can replicate Sir Alex Ferguson’s success as he pays tribute to his former boss on the 40th anniversary of his appointment; Watch Man Utd vs Aston Villa live on Sky ; kick-off at 4.30pm this Sunday William Bitibiri Football Journalist @williambitibiri Friday 6 November 2026 16:19, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Micheal Carrick says ‘success takes time’ and won’t rule out giving Manchester United the same success as Sir Alex Ferguson Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can reach the heights achieved under Sir Alex Ferguson but is not expecting the same level of patience. Friday marks 40 years since Ferguson was appointed United manager on November 6, 1986. It is an anniversary that comes at a particularly significant moment for the club, with Carrick's position in charge still facing intense scrutiny. United's dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in midweek offered Carrick some much-needed breathing space after a nine-game winless run, but Sunday's Premier League clash against Aston Villa, live on Sky, represents another significant test.
